answer: Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique proof-of-work cipher bound to its reputation slot; forging a duplicate identity forces repeating the full stake plus compute cost, which scales linearly with every fake node. Reputation decays toward a nadir when corroborating peers vanish, so a sybil cluster isolated in the ocean of honest nodes earns nothing and loses its locked stake. Attack cost therefore exceeds any marginal reward, making mass identity creation economically irrational. The once0003 deployment anchors trust at qQ5qYhr7nH.
